note: #3066 asks for DXC's disassembly to print human-readable forms instead of raw values. The symptom is a PRESENCE (raw value still printed) wrapped around an ABSENCE (nothing decodes it), so both vacuity directions are guarded. Clauses 1-2 are the SELF-TEST: they require a complete disassembly listing (a named row in the Resource Bindings table) and require the existing opcode annotator to have run and decoded a hard-coded value ('; FMax(a,b)', the reporter's own baseline in the issue body). A failed compile, a stripped module or a dead annotator therefore scores NO-MATCH rather than manufacturing a clean absence. Clauses 3-6 each pin one whole LINE with a '$' anchor, so the comment must stop exactly where it stops today: (3) ask B, the float constant is still LLVM hex 0x3F1A36E2E0000000 and the comment does not restate 0.0001; (4) ask C, the storeOutput comment names its operands but does not resolve their VALUES (sigId 0 -> SV_Target, component i8 0 -> .x) - this clause also positively demonstrates that the op-name half of ask C is already satisfied; (5) ask D, the store's handle operand is an anonymous '%<digits>' and the comment names no resource; (6) ask E, the ViewID output-dependency rows are bare scalar indices, digits only. CONTROLS, all captured in this directory. Clauses 3, 4 and 5 all stop matching, which is the proof this predicate is not satisfied by a disassembly that prints the value by name. (c) control-plain.hlsl (expect no-match): a valid shader with none of the constructs - proves the predicate is not satisfied by any successful compile.
